computations.definition: s = sqrt( mean over the training items i of ||z_i||_2^2 ), the RMS of the per-item latent VECTOR NORM (not a per-coordinate RMS, which would be ||z||_2/sqrt(D) and would multiply the tanh argument by sqrt(D)). It is measured once at step 0 and frozen. rho = 0.5 is the fixed ratio of the latent scale to the ball radius: rho = s/R_c, so R_c = s/rho = 2s; the curvature is c = (rho/s)^2 = 0.25/s^2 (units 1/||.||^2). c is never an input and never tuned. FAIL-CLOSED: if s is not finite or s <= 0 the run stops with an error; s is never replaced by a default, because a silent default would change the curvature the mechanism claims.
inputs: the baseline encoder's latents z_i (train items, D-dim) at step 0
computations.name: scale
computations.note: measured on the training split at step 0 only; frozen
computations.output: s (a scalar) and the curvature c = (rho/s)^2

computations.definition: LIFT(v) = tanh(sqrt(c)*||v||) * v / (sqrt(c)*||v|| + eps) with eps = 1e-12, and LIFT(0) = 0 because the numerator v vanishes (the eps guard only keeps the division finite; there is NO separate zero-norm branch). At c = 0 LIFT is the identity map (the GEOMETRY_OFF arm). The lift is applied to the residual and to the codebook vector SEPARATELY, never to their difference.
inputs: a residual r (B, D) or a codebook vector a (K1, D)
computations.name: lift
computations.output: the lifted point u = LIFT(r) or q = LIFT(a)

computations.definition: MOBIUS(x,y) = ((1 + 2c<x,y> + c||y||^2)x + (1 - c||x||^2)y) / (1 + 2c<x,y> + c^2||x||^2||y||^2 + eps); DIST(x,y) = (2/sqrt(c)) * artanh( min( sqrt(c)*||MOBIUS(-x,y)||, 1 - 1e-6 ) ), the idea's exact expression, with the clamp as the ONLY numerical guard on the artanh argument (the lift approaches the ball boundary as tanh -> 1, so a float latent can round onto it). eps = 1e-12 appears in the Mobius denominator only; the norm carries no eps. At c = 0, DIST(x,y) = 2||x - y||.
computations.domain: c > 0 for the curved arm; both arguments lifted, so c||x||^2 < 1 and c||y||^2 < 1
computations.name: distance
computations.note: the idea's expression, with the eps in the Mobius denominator and the min(., 1 - 1e-6) clamp on the artanh argument, exactly as the SymPy surface states

computations.definition: D_k = DIST(u, q_k); score_k = D_k - off_k. The curvature supplies D_k, the behaviour side supplies off_k, and score_k cannot be formed without both.
computations.name: level-1 score
computations.note: the single coupling surface: the executable statements carry it end to end (lift, distance, demand, weight, offset, score, assignment, residual)

computations.definition: k1 = argmin_k score_k, ties resolved to the smallest k. The assignment is discrete; the encoder gradient reaches the model through the baseline's straight-through estimator on the chosen code, exactly as in the baseline.
computations.name: level-1 assignment

computations.definition: r_next = r - a_{k1}: the unmodified baseline codeword vector, not LIFT(a_{k1}) and not the offset-adjusted position. The recursion's CODE is the baseline's; its input r_next differs from the baseline's only because the level-1 choice differs. LIFT(a_{k1}) enters only inside score_k.
inputs: the chosen UNLIFTED codebook vector a_{k1}
computations.name: residual recursion
computations.output: r_next (B, D), the input of level 2

computations.definition: From TRAINING-SPLIT sessions only: directed counts t_ij for consecutive pairs (i consumed before j, self-pairs dropped); out_i = sum_j t_ij and in_j = sum_i t_ij are that graph's degrees; eps = 1e-12. m_i = sum_j [ t_ij / sqrt(out_i * in_j + eps) ] over j = 1..N (the summation is INSIDE, so the value is well defined). Per epoch, with the CURRENT level-1 codes of the training items, a minibatch of B items gives p_ik = softmax_k(-D_ik / tau) with tau = 1, shape (B, K1). The epoch aggregate sums over ALL N training items: num_k = sum over the batches of (p_ik * m_i[:, None]).sum(0) and den_k = sum over the batches of p_ik.sum(0), then b_raw_epoch_k = num_k / (den_k + eps), shape (K1,) - an item-weighted mean, never a mean of per-batch means. Then, ONCE PER EPOCH at the end of the epoch, b_raw <- (1 - eta) * b_raw + eta * b_raw_epoch, eta = 0.1, initialised to 1 for every codeword, detached and no_grad; b_k = log(1 + b_raw_k / mean_k(b_raw_k)). The soft assignment p_ik uses D_ik, the PURE geodesic distance, not score_k: that is the idea's definition of the behaviour channel. Because b_raw holds its initial value 1 until the first end-of-epoch update, EVERY epoch-1 batch has b_raw = 1 for all k, hence b_k = log 2 for all k and a k-independent offset; the offsets separate only from epoch 2. The EMA applies to b_raw, never to b_k.
inputs: the training-split consecutive-pair count matrix t_ij (N, N)
the current level-1 soft assignment p_ik (N, K1) of the training items
computations.name: behaviour demand
computations.note: training split only; no validation, test or future behaviour

computations.definition: The specification COMPLETES the idea here: the idea fixes mean_scale as the epoch-1 running mean of min_k D_k and says nothing about w during epoch 1, when that mean does not exist yet. The completion is w = 0 during epoch 1 (hence off_k = 0 and a pure geodesic assignment), which is immaterial to the score because the epoch-1 offsets are k-independent anyway. mean_scale = the ITEM-WEIGHTED mean of min_k D_k over the training items of epoch 1 (not a mean of per-batch means), in the CURRENT branch's distance (the Euclidean 2||u-q|| when GEOMETRY_OFF, so the switch stays scale-consistent), FROZEN from epoch 2 on. From epoch 2 on, w = rho_off * mean_scale / max_k log(1 + b_k) with rho_off = 0.10 (documented default), recomputed at the END of every epoch from the frozen mean_scale and that epoch's b_k and held constant during the next epoch, in step with the b_raw update.
inputs: min_k D_k of every training item of epoch 1 (the source of mean_scale)
num_k and den_k accumulated over the training items of epoch 1
computations.name: offset weight
computations.note: no constant is swept: mean_scale is measured once, rho_off is the proposal's documented default
computations.output: w, recomputed at the END of every epoch from the frozen mean_scale and that epoch's b_k, then held constant during the next epoch

computations.definition: off_k = w * log(1 + b_k) with b_k from 'behaviour demand' (NOT b_raw_k: using b_raw would change both the offset scale and w's normaliser). During epoch 1 this is 0 because w = 0. With BEHAVIOUR_OFF the implementation sets off_k = 0 for every k on the FLAG itself, never on a computed maximum.
computations.name: offset
computations.note: the b consumed by score_k, off_k and max_k log(1+b_k) is b_k

computations.definition: loss = baseline_recon + baseline_commit, byte-identical to the baseline, with the straight-through estimator on the chosen code. The mechanism adds NO new loss term: it changes which codeword is chosen, so the baseline objective trains a different quantisation and the encoder gradient flows through the baseline's reconstruct-path STE on a_{k1} exactly once.
inputs: the baseline reconstruction and commitment terms
computations.name: objective
computations.note: no auxiliary loss, no extra optimiser
computations.output: the scalar loss the baseline optimiser minimises

executable_statements: def lift(v, c): return v if c == 0.0 else v * (torch.tanh(math.sqrt(c) * _norm(v)) / (math.sqrt(c) * _norm(v) + eps)).unsqueeze(-1)

def mobius(x, y, c): return ((1 + 2 * c * (x * y).sum(-1, keepdim=True) + c * (y * y).sum(-1, keepdim=True)) * x + (1 - c * (x * x).sum(-1, keepdim=True)) * y) / (1 + 2 * c * (x * y).sum(-1, keepdim=True) + c * c * (x * x).sum(-1, keepdim=True) * (y * y).sum(-1, keepdim=True) + eps)
def dist(x, y, c): return 2.0 * _norm(x - y) if c == 0.0 else (2.0 / math.sqrt(c)) * torch.atanh(torch.clamp(math.sqrt(c) * _norm(mobius(-x, y, c)), max=1.0 - 1e-6))
num_k = torch.zeros(K1); den_k = torch.zeros(K1)   # the epoch's accumulators
num_k = num_k + (p_ik * m_i[:, None]).sum(0)        # one batch
b_raw_epoch_k = num_k / (den_k + eps)              # once, at the epoch's end
b_raw = (1 - eta) * b_raw + eta * b_raw_epoch_k    # the carried buffer
mean_scale = ms_sum / ms_count                     # frozen from epoch 2
w = 0.0 if (BEHAVIOUR_OFF or epoch == 1) else rho_off * mean_scale / torch.log1p(b_k).max()
off_k = 0.0 if BEHAVIOUR_OFF else w * torch.log1p(b_k)
continuous_surface.note: The statements are the DISTANCE in SymPy: they are the equations the reference contract must equal, statement by statement. The executable_statements are the same surface as a program: the lift, the distance, the demand's accumulation, the weight and the score, in the order the trainer runs them. The carried buffers (b_raw, ms_sum, ms_count) live across the epoch and are stated here with the values they carry.

conventions.curvature: the ball is of curvature kappa = -c with c > 0; the ball radius is R_c = 1/sqrt(c) - a radius R with kappa = -1/R^2 is the same family under c = 1/R^2, and every distance, exponential map and radius must use ONE of them
conventions.distance: d_c(x, y) = (2/sqrt(c)) artanh(sqrt(c) ||(-x) (+) y||), with (+) the canonical Mobius sum; at c = 0 the limit is 2||x - y||, and the factor 2 is the metric's normalisation
conventions.exponential_map: exp_0^c(v) = tanh(sqrt(c)||v||) v / (sqrt(c)||v||), and exp_x^c(v) = x (+) [tanh(sqrt(c) lambda_x^c ||v|| / 2) v / (sqrt(c)||v||)] with lambda_x^c = 2/(1 - c||x||^2)
conventions.fréchet_mean: the Frechet mean of a weighted set is the point minimising the weighted sum of squared distances; a coordinate average may not be called a Frechet mean
conventions.source: tools/research/contracts/HYPERBOLIC_GEOMETRY_CONTRACT.md, which the implementation must cite and the reviewers must check
conventions.straight_through: the assignment is an argmin and has no gradient; the reconstruction gradient reaches the encoder through the straight-through estimator x_q = x + (x_q - x).detach()
conventions.tangent_norm: a tangent vector's Euclidean coordinate norm is not its Riemannian norm: ||v||_{0,c} = lambda_0^c ||v|| = 2||v||, so d_c(0, exp_0^c(v)) = 2||v|| and log_0^c(exp_0^c(v)) = v

spec.conventions_derived_by: the framework: the canonical geometry contract

dimensions.m_i: N, the per training item mass
dimensions.p_ik: B x K1 for one minibatch; num_k and den_k aggregate it over the N epoch items
dimensions.t_ij: N x N over all N training items

excluded: any use of validation, test or future behaviour in the demand
any learned profile, attention, or per-codeword curvature parameter
any denoising or autoencoding pretraining; the RQ-VAE trains as baseline
any extra loss term, auxiliary head or second geometry
any sweep, ablation training run or seed repetition

gradient_rules.operator: the mechanism's constants (rho, s, c, rho_off, eta, tau)
gradient_rules.rule: no gradient: they are constants, and b_raw and mean_scale are detached buffers, so no mechanism quantity is learned
the argmin has no gradient; the reconstruction gradient reaches the encoder through the baseline's straight-through estimator on the chosen code a_{k1}
trained exactly as the baseline trains it; the distance and the offset never appear in a differentiable loss, they only select k1

encoder_gradient: perturbing a training item's feature must change the encoder's gradient through the reconstruction path's straight-through estimator on a_{k1}, and must not change it when only that STE link is removed; the baseline commitment term keeps its own gradient and is not part of this test

inputs: r, the residual entering level 1 (B, D) - the baseline's r
the level-1 codebook a (K1, D) - the baseline's, learned, never detached
the training-split counts t_ij (N, N) and the per-item mass m_i (N,), train only
the demand b_raw (K1,) carried across epochs, detached, no_grad
the frozen scale s, curvature c and mean_scale
spec.mechanism: The level-1 codeword choice of the baseline RQ-VAE is re-scored by a fixed derived Poincare distance minus a frozen train-only behaviour offset: the offset turns each level-1 codeword into a popularity-adjusted directed-transition surplus (a PMI-style m_i aggregated by the soft level-1 assignment), normalised to its own mean, and weighted by a geodesic scale measured once in epoch 1. The curvature is not swept: c = (rho/s)^2 with rho = 0.5 the proposal's fixed dimensionless radius-to-scale ratio and s the training-split RMS of the per-item latent NORM measured at step 0. The CODE of levels 2 and 3, of the residual recursion, of the reconstruction codebook and of the straight-through estimator is byte-identical to the baseline (their INPUTS differ, because the level-1 choice differs); reconstruction uses the UNLIFTED codeword a_{k1}. The behaviour channel and the curvature act on one expression, score_k = DIST(LIFT(r), LIFT(a_k)) - off_k.
outputs: k1, the level-1 codeword index for every residual (B,)
the demand b_k (K1,) and the offset off_k (K1,) as diagnostics
parameters: rho = 0.5, the fixed ratio of the latent scale to the ball radius (R_c = s/rho = 2s)
s = the training-split RMS of the per-item latent norm at step 0; c = (rho/s)^2
rho_off = 0.10, the proposal's documented offset strength
eta = 0.1, the demand EMA momentum; tau = 1, the soft assignment temperature
the demand buffer b_raw (K1,): detached, no_grad, initialised to one and updated once per epoch (NOT frozen)
the frozen mean_scale: the item-weighted mean of min_k D_k over epoch 1, constant from epoch 2
switches: BEHAVIOUR_OFF (present in code, never trained): m_i = 1 for every item, so b_raw_k = sum_i p_ik / (sum_i p_ik + eps) = 1 to within eps for every k (not exactly 1), b_k = log 2 to within eps for every k, and the offset would be a k-INDEPENDENT constant to within eps - a constant shift cannot change argmin_k score_k. The implementation therefore sets off_k = 0 exactly, on the FLAG, so the assignment is pure geodesic nearest neighbour in the derived ball.

GEOMETRY_OFF (present in code, never trained): c = 0, so LIFT is the identity and DIST(x,y) = 2||x - y||; the score is 2||r - a_k|| - w*log(1 + b_k). The demand stays ENABLED but is recomputed from the Euclidean distances (p_ik = softmax_k(-2||u-q_k||/tau), hence b_raw and b_k change), and mean_scale is the EUCLIDEAN item-weighted mean of min_k 2||u-q_k|| over epoch 1, so w stays scale-consistent.

BOTH_ON: the single formal run - c = (rho/s)^2 with the lift and the geodesic distance, plus the frozen train-only offset with its derived weight. Trained once: no sweep, no seed repetition, no early stopping.

training_integration.loss: baseline_recon + baseline_commit, unchanged, straight-through on a_{k1}

papers.abstract: The success of models operating on tokenized data has heightened the need for effective tokenization methods, particularly in vision and auditory tasks where inputs are naturally continuous. A common solution is to employ Vector Quantization (VQ) within VQ Variational Autoencoders (VQVAEs), transforming inputs into discrete tokens by clustering embeddings in Euclidean space. However, Euclidean embeddings not only suffer from inefficient packing and limited separation - due to their polynomial volume growth - but are also prone to codebook collapse, where only a small subset of codebook vectors are effectively utilized. To address these limitations, we introduce HyperVQ, a novel approach that formulates VQ as a hyperbolic Multinomial Logistic Regression (MLR) problem, leveraging the exponential volume growth in hyperbolic space to mitigate collapse and improve cluster separability. Additionally, HyperVQ represents codebook vectors as geometric representatives of hyperbolic decision hyperplanes, encouraging disentangled and robust latent representations. Our experiments demonstrate that HyperVQ matches traditional VQ in generative and reconstruction tasks, while surpassing it in disc

papers.abstract: Residual Vector Quantization turns continuous representations into discrete, multi-level token sequences. Yet most methods operate in Euclidean space, despite the coarse-to-fine structure of the resulting codes and the latent hierarchies present in many data domains. papers.abstract: Most high-performance block-coding systems for image compression, such as JPEG, have been designed for software or dedicated digital hardware implementations where the data are already assumed to be available in digital format. In modern CMOS photosensors, smart-pixel technologies have allowed the realization of basic signal processing tasks at the pixel level, in analog format before analog-to-digital (A/D) conversion. The elimination of A/D converters and implementation of block-coding directly over analog blocks of pixels in such sensors can be attractive both in terms of area savings and power consumption. papers.abstract: Vector quantization is a technique in machine learning that discretizes continuous representations into a set of discrete vectors. It is widely employed in tokenizing data representations for large language models, diffusion models, and other generative models. Despite its prevalence, the characteristics and behaviors of vector quantization in generative models remain largely underexplored. In this study, we investigate representation collapse in vector quantization - a critical degradation where codebook tokens or latent embeddings lose their discriminative power by converging to a limited subset of values. This collapse fundamentally compromises the model's ability to capture diverse data patterns. By leveraging both synthetic and real datasets, we identify the severity of each type of collapses and triggering conditions. Our analysis reveals that restricted initialization and limited encoder capacity result in tokens collapse and embeddings collapse. Building on these findings, we propose potential solutions aimed at mitigating each collapse. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first comprehensive study examining representation collapsing problems in vector quantization.
papers.title: Representation Collapsing Problems in Vector Quantization

papers.abstract: Machine learning algorithms have been shown to be highly effective in solving optimization problems in a wide range of applications. Such algorithms typically use gradient descent with backpropagation and the chain rule. Hence, the backpropagation fails if intermediate gradients are zero for some functions in the computational graph, because it causes the gradients to collapse when multiplying with zero. Vector quantization is one of those challenging functions for machine learning algorithms, since it is a piece-wise constant function and its gradient is zero almost everywhere. A typical solution is to apply the straight through estimator which simply copies the gradients over the vector quantization function in the backpropagation. Other solutions are based on smooth or stochastic approximation. This study proposes a vector quantization technique called NSVQ, which approximates the vector quantization behavior by substituting a multiplicative noise so that it can be used for machine learning problems. papers.abstract: The success of models operating on tokenized data has heightened the need for effective tokenization methods, particularly in vision and auditory tasks where inputs are naturally continuous. A common solution is to employ Vector Quantization (VQ) within VQ Variational Autoencoders (VQVAEs), transforming inputs into discrete tokens by clustering embeddings in Euclidean space. However, Euclidean embeddings not only suffer from inefficient packing and limited separation - due to their polynomial volume growth - but are also prone to codebook collapse, where only a small subset of codebook vectors are effectively utilized. To address these limitations, we introduce HyperVQ, a novel approach that formulates VQ as a hyperbolic Multinomial Logistic Regression (MLR) problem, leveraging the exponential volume growth in hyperbolic space to mitigate collapse and improve cluster separability. Additionally, HyperVQ represents codebook vectors as geometric representatives of hyperbolic decision hyperplanes, encouraging disentangled and robust latent representations. Our experiments demonstrate that HyperVQ matches traditional VQ in generative and reconstruction tasks, while surpassing it in disc

papers.abstract: We present a novel vector quantization (VQ) module for the two state-of-the-art long-range simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) algorithms. The VQ task in SLAM is generally performed using unsupervised methods. We provide an alternative approach trough embedding a semisupervised hyperbolic graph convolutional neural network (HGCN) in the VQ step of the SLAM processes. The SLAM platforms we have utilized for this purpose are fast appearance-based mapping (FABMAP) and oriented fast and rotated short (ORB), both of which rely on extracting the features of the captured images in their loop closure detection (LCD) module. For the first time, we have considered the space formed by these SURF features, robust image descriptors, as a graph, enabling us to apply an HGCN in the VQ section which results in an improved LCD performance. The HGCN vector quantizes the SURF feature space, leading to a bag-of-word (BoW) representation construction of the images. This representation is subsequently used to determine LCD accuracy and recall. Our approaches in this study are referred to as HGCN-FABMAP and HGCN-ORB. papers.abstract: Residual Vector Quantization turns continuous representations into discrete, multi-level token sequences. Yet most methods operate in Euclidean space, despite the coarse-to-fine structure of the resulting codes and the latent hierarchies present in many data domains. Hyperbolic geometry offers a natural alternative for hierarchical representations, but naive hyperbolic extensions introduce geometric inconsistencies: non-associative hyperbolic addition prevents consistent residual aggregation, while standard straight-through gradient estimation ignores the geometry of the latent space. We propose a geometry-aware hyperbolic residual quantization that addresses these issues in both the forward and backward passes. In the forward pass, Hyperbolic Residual Aggregation restores the telescoping behavior of residual quantization on the Poincare ball. In the backward pass, a discounted Hyperbolic Straight-Through Estimator routes the reconstruction gradient through the quantizer as a single geometric block, avoiding unstable recursive gradient transport across residual stages. papers.abstract: Most high-performance block-coding systems for image compression, such as JPEG, have been designed for software or dedicated digital hardware implementations where the data are already assumed to be available in digital format. In modern CMOS photosensors, smart-pixel technologies have allowed the realization of basic signal processing tasks at the pixel level, in analog format before analog-to-digital (A/D) conversion. The elimination of A/D converters and implementation of block-coding directly over analog blocks of pixels in such sensors can be attractive both in terms of area savings and power consumption. The design of block encoders, under the strong hardware constraints that derive from the A/D converter removal, has been investigated in this paper. papers.abstract: Vector quantization is a technique in machine learning that discretizes continuous representations into a set of discrete vectors. It is widely employed in tokenizing data representations for large language models, diffusion models, and other generative models. Despite its prevalence, the characteristics and behaviors of vector quantization in generative models remain largely underexplored. In this study, we investigate representation collapse in vector quantization - a critical degradation where codebook tokens or latent embeddings lose their discriminative power by converging to a limited subset of values. This collapse fundamentally compromises the model's ability to capture diverse data patterns. By leveraging both synthetic and real datasets, we identify the severity of each type of collapses and triggering conditions. Our analysis reveals that restricted initialization and limited encoder capacity result in tokens collapse and embeddings collapse. Building on these findings, we propose potential solutions aimed at mitigating each collapse. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first comprehensive study examining representation collapsing problems in vector quantization.
papers.title: Representation Collapsing Problems in Vector Quantization

papers.abstract: Machine learning algorithms have been shown to be highly effective in solving optimization problems in a wide range of applications. Such algorithms typically use gradient descent with backpropagation and the chain rule. Hence, the backpropagation fails if intermediate gradients are zero for some functions in the computational graph, because it causes the gradients to collapse when multiplying with zero. Vector quantization is one of those challenging functions for machine learning algorithms, since it is a piece-wise constant function and its gradient is zero almost everywhere. A typical solution is to apply the straight through estimator which simply copies the gradients over the vector quantization function in the backpropagation. Other solutions are based on smooth or stochastic approximation. This study proposes a vector quantization technique called NSVQ, which approximates the vector quantization behavior by substituting a multiplicative noise so that it can be used for machine learning problems. progress_records.content: STEP 1 — goal: scope/spec audit of the five proposals against the contract (behaviour signal, curved op, real coupling, three switches, derived constants, one-run cost). Read: the five proposal texts and the per-idea evidence bundles (BEHAVIORAL_EVIDENCE E1-E3 PROPOSED, GEOMETRIC_NECESSITY E12-E13 PROPOSED, plus shared OBSERVED E5-E11). Observed: all five pass the scope gate (each names a training-only transition-demand signal, an explicit exp_0/Mobius/artanh Poincare distance in the level-1 argmin, and both switches that reduce EXACTLY to baseline: behaviour-off -> offset 0, geometry-off -> c=0 -> Euclidean). Differences that matter for ranking: (a) COUPLING DEPTH — closed per-step loop (demand measured through the same curved soft assignment then subtracted from that curved distance) in l1pdo-rq, DEMARGIN-L1-CURV and BEABLATE-CURVSCALE; frozen pre-computed tables in pmi-geomargin-l1-rq and GEOMARGIN-L1-RQ. (b) CONSTANT HYGIENE — offset scale measured in the same units as d_c in DEMARGIN (mean geodesic half-margin) and BEABLATE (0.25*s_D, s_D = mean min_k D_k), 0.10 of an epoch-1 measured scale in pmi and 0.10*Dbar/rms(z) in GEOMARGIN, but l1pdo uses w = beta = 0.25, the baseline commitment weight that multiplies a SQUARED residual, applied to a length — dimensionally borrowed. (c) STABILITY — l1pdo's offset is centred and clipped to +/-ln3*0.25 (bounded, symmetric); DEMARGIN's is one-sided, clamp[0,3w] on a mean-normalised heavy-tailed demand; BEABLATE's EMA lambda = 1/72000 over a 72,000-step budget leaves demand near 1 for most of training. Still open: which of these differences the frozen evidence actually rewards.

STEP 2 — goal: ground each proposal in the shared OBSERVED evidence. Read: E5-E11 of every bundle (identical content). 5. DEMARGIN-L1-CURV - ranked last because its offset scale w = mean_i[(max_k D_ik - min_k D_ik)/2] is the full nearest-to-farthest distance half-spread, far larger than the local nearest-code margin, and the offset is clamped to [0, 3w] and hence one-sided: it is the largest and least controlled displacement of the five, the regime E6 shows is destructive (l1_br 0.04671 vs baseline 0.0555, and E8 caps the K=256 first-level share at 0.0822); it also admits frozen s drift toward the ball boundary where atanh explodes.

bserved recalls (l1_only 0.06233, l1_br_euclid 0.06207, resample 0.06363) come from arms with no behaviour term and no curvature, while behaviour-geodesic level-1 arms sit at 0.0546-0.0550; E8 additionally caps the K=256 first-level pair-sharing rate at 0.0822. So a level-1-only curved behaviour margin has bounded headroom below the 0.065 target, and the top-ranked candidate's 10%-of-typical-distance cap may be too small to flip enough assignments to beat single-seed noise, with no ablation, sweep or seed repetition permitted to establish which term acted.

progress_records.content: STEP 1 — goal: scope/spec audit of the five proposals against the contract (behaviour signal, curved op, real coupling, three switches, derived constants, one-run cost). Read: the five proposal texts and the per-idea evidence bundles (BEHAVIORAL_EVIDENCE E1-E3 PROPOSED, GEOMETRIC_NECESSITY E12-E13 PROPOSED, plus shared OBSERVED E5-E11). Observed: all five pass the scope gate (each names a training-only transition-demand signal, an explicit exp_0/Mobius/artanh Poincare distance in the level-1 argmin, and both switches that reduce EXACTLY to baseline: behaviour-off -> offset 0, geometry-off -> c=0 -> Euclidean). Differences that matter for ranking: (a) COUPLING DEPTH — closed per-step loop (demand measured through the same curved soft assignment then subtracted from that curved distance) in l1pdo-rq, DEMARGIN-L1-CURV and BEABLATE-CURVSCALE; frozen pre-computed tables in pmi-geomargin-l1-rq and GEOMARGIN-L1-RQ. (b) CONSTANT HYGIENE — offset scale measured in the same units as d_c in DEMARGIN (mean geodesic half-margin) and BEABLATE (0.25*s_D, s_D = mean min_k D_k), 0.10 of an epoch-1 measured scale in pmi and 0.10*Dbar/rms(z) in GEOMARGIN, but l1pdo uses w = beta = 0.25, the baseline commitment weight that multiplies a SQUARED residual, applied to a length — dimensionally borrowed. (c) STABILITY — l1pdo's offset is centred and clipped to +/-ln3*0.25 (bounded, symmetric); DEMARGIN's is one-sided, clamp[0,3w] on a mean-normalised heavy-tailed demand; BEABLATE's EMA lambda = 1/72000 over a 72,000-step budget leaves demand near 1 for most of training. Still open: which of these differences the frozen evidence actually rewards.

STEP 2 — goal: ground each proposal in the shared OBSERVED evidence. Read: E5-E11 of every bundle (identical content). Observations: E6/E7 beam survival and teacher-forced NLL: the hyperbolic level-1 variant l1_br already DEGENERATED in the probes (T1 NLL 0.00, T4 NLL 9.03, recall@10 0.04671), while Euclidean level-1 variants reached l1_br_euclid 0.06207, l1_only 0.06233 and the best observed 0.06363 (resample, which buys its gain at depth 3-4: T3 NLL 0.73, T4 0.05, gold prefix alive depth4 0.088). So (i) a level-1-only mechanism inherits a family base rate that has so far failed to pass 0.065, and (ii) the documented failure mode of a curved level-1 assignment is first-token mass collapse (T1 NLL = 0.00), which one-sided/unbounded demand attractors risk repeating. E6 also shows gold-prefix survival at depth 1 is already 1.000 for l1_br_euclid/l1_only, so the gain must come from compressing levels 2-3, not from token-1 accuracy. E8: share of canonical pairs sharing a K=256 level-1 code is only 0.0822 (permuted -0.0129) against 0.3106 at K=16 -> there IS headroom for behaviour-aligned level-1 co-location; E11: same_first_prefix_rate 0.0907 vs permuted null 0.067 shows the current prefix carries almost no behavioural information. E5/E10: demand is highly skewed (top-1 successor mass 0.4375 in the low-entropy quintile; mean out-degree 5.45, median branch 3), which is the concrete argument for popularity adjustment and against unbounded offsets. Still open: final ordering.

STEP 3 — final answer (complete, stands alone).

RANK: l1pdo-rq | position=1 | reason=Only proposal combining a genuine closed geometry->behaviour->geometry loop (per-codeword demand built from the same curved softmax whose distance the offset then shifts) with a bounded, mean-centred offset (clipped at +/-ln3*0.25), which is the form the evidence says is needed: E7 shows the curved level-1 arm l1_br collapsed first-token mass (T1 NLL 0.00, recall 0.04671), so a symmetric bounded offset is the safest way to use the level-1 headroom of E8 (0.0822 of canonical pairs share a K=256 code vs 0.3106 at K=16) without repeating that collapse; its one defect is w = beta = 0.25 borrowed from the squared-residual commitment term.
RANK: DEMARGIN-L1-CURV | position=2 | reason=Same closed loop and the best-derived offset scale of the five (w = measured mean geodesic half-margin, T = w, both in the units actually subtracted from d_c), so the behaviour/geometry balance is not an arbitrary constant; but its offset is one-sided, clamp[0,3w] on a mean-normalised demand that E5/E10 show is heavy-tailed (top-1 successor mass 0.4375, mean out-degree 5.45), which is exactly the hub-attractor that produced the l1_br degeneration in E7; ranked second, not first, on that stability difference alone.
RANK: pmi-geomargin-l1-rq | position=3 | reason=Its behaviour statistic is the best matched to the evidence — a degree-normalised (PMI-style) transition surplus, which directly counters the hub dominance visible in E5/E10 and the near-chance behavioural content of the prefix in E11 (0.0907 vs permuted 0.067), and its offset is bounded at 0.10 of a measured epoch-1 scale; it drops below the closed-loop pair because b_k is a frozen table so the geometry never feeds back into the behaviour term, and c = (0.5/s)^2 puts typical items at ball norm ~0.46, i.e. close to the Euclidean regime its own risk list flags.
RANK: GEOMARGIN-L1-RQ | position=4 | reason=Cleanest switch algebra of the five (zero-mean margin, so behaviour-off is literally the baseline argmin) and a derived weight w = 0.1*Dbar/rms(z); but z is built in a frozen pre-pass from frozen hard level-1 assignments, so the coupling is single-shot and stale relative to the moving encoder (its own stated risk), and the margin cap of 10% of the typical geodesic distance is the kind of nudge that E6/E7's flat 0.0550 successor_geodesic_coarse and tangent_successor_residual results suggest does not move recall.
RANK: BEABLATE-CURVSCALE-RQ | position=5 | reason=Dimensionally the tidiest offset (w*s_D with s_D the measured mean min_k D_k, hence curvature-invariant) but lambda = 1/72000 over the frozen 72,000-step budget leaves demand within a few percent of 1 for most of training and caps the competing part of the offset at 0.25*s_D, with c = 0.25 placing typical ball norm at ~0.23 (near-Euclidean); that makes it the arm most likely to be statistically indistinguishable from baseline in a single run, which E6's 0.0555-0.0638 spread says is fatal for a 0.065 target.

OBJECTION: All five proposals act only on the level-1 argmin, yet the frozen evidence shows the gold level-1 prefix is already alive at depth 1 for the Euclidean level-1 variants (1.000 for l1_br_euclid/l1_only, E6) and that the observed recall spread is won or lost at depths 3-4 (resample 0.06363 with T3/T4 NLL 0.73/0.05, E7), so the round's mechanism may be capped below 0.065 by attacking a non-binding constraint; and the one curved level-1 arm already run (l1_
br) degenerated to T1 NLL 0.00 / recall 0.04671, so any one-sided demand offset risks reproducing that collapse and a single run cannot separate that failure from seed noise.

(b) E7 teacher-forced NLL: l1_br T1/T2/T3 = 0.00/0.00/0.00, l1_br_euclid 0.00/3.22/4.36. (c) E8 first-level capacity ceiling on frozen Stage1 vectors: share of canonical pairs sharing a K cluster = 0.3106 (K=16), 0.1547 (K=64), 0.0822 (K=256). (d) E5 successor-entropy stratification: top-1 successor mass 0.4375 in the lowest quintile vs 0.0543 in the highest, Spearman -0.973, so the transition mass is heavily skewed toward a few successors. (e) E9 cohort-profile signal: positive shares a successor cohort with its anchor 0.9291 vs 0.8871 for negatives, 0.5898 of pairs beat all ten negatives. (f) E10/E11: 118315 train edges, mean out-degree 5.45; baseline same-first-prefix rate 0.0907 vs permuted null 0.067.
REASONING: all five proposals are the same mechanism class - keep K1=256, lift the level-1 residual and the baseline level-1 codebook into a Poincare ball, score with d_c, and subtract a detached per-codeword behaviour offset before the argmin, leaving levels 2-3, the loss and the STE at baseline. So they must be separated on (i) how the offset is scaled in distance units, (ii) whether the behaviour statistic is popularity-debiased, (iii) whether curvature is strong enough not to be a no-op, (iv) collapse risk under a single run. E6 shows that mild/coarse geodesic-successor level-1 arms scored 0.0546-0.0550, i.e. at/below baseline, and that the best frozen arms (0.0621-0.0636) used neither behaviour nor curvature, so aggressive one-sided level-1 displacement (l1_br 0.0467) is the demonstrated failure mode. Best scale is therefore an offset tied to the measured mean nearest-code geodesic distance, not to the full distance spread. That puts pmi-geomargin (10% of mean min_k D_k, doubly popularity-adjusted, online surplus refresh) first, l1pdo-rq second (live curved-softmax loop and c=1 so curvature is not near-Euclidean, zero-mean symmetric offset), BEABLATE third (correct curved-unit scaling but c=0.25 and lambda=1/72000 make it near-static and near-Euclidean), GEOMARGIN fourth (zero-mean margin is clean but z is frozen from BASELINE Euclidean assignments and c=1 with a 10% cap is likely a no-op), DEMARGIN last (offset scale = mean half-spread, clamped to 0..3w, the largest and one-sided displacement, plus admitted atanh boundary risk).
STILL OPEN: none of these touches depth 2/3, where E6/E7 locate the loss for the strongest frozen arms (l1_br_euclid 0.829/0.161), and E8 caps the K=256 first-level share at 0.0822; that is the objection recorded with the ranking. Next record carries
the complete answer.

All five bundles share E4-E11; only E12/E13 and some E10 contents differ.
OBSERVED (shared evidence, decisive): [E6] width-20 beam survival on 57,439 test rows - l1_br (pure hyperbolic level 1) recall@10 0.04671 vs l1_br_euclid 0.06207, l1_only 0.06233, resample 0.06363; [E7] teacher-forced NLL - l1_br T4 NLL 9.03 vs euclid 1.23; [E8] first-level capacity ceiling - canonical pairs sharing a K=256 cluster only 0.0822 (negatives 0.0129), K=64 0.1547, K=16 0.3106; [E11] existing baseline same_first_prefix_rate 0.0907 vs permuted null 0.067; [E5] successor entropy is strongly structured (top-1 mass 0.4375 low-entropy quintile vs 0.0543 high, Spearman -0.973); [E9] train-only cohort-profile signal is real (positive shares successor cohort 0.9291 vs 0.8871 negatives, profile overlap beats all ten negatives in 0.5898 of pairs); BEABLATE has an extra E10 (mean branch entropy 1.1081 nats, median branch degree 3).
REASONING: All five are the same mechanism family (level-1 Poincare distance minus a behaviour-demand offset, levels 2-3/loss/STE untouched), so placement turns on (a) whether the offset weight is derived in geodesic distance units, (b) whether the behaviour statistic is computed through the curved assignment (loop strength), (c) how stiff the curvature is, and (d) collapse risk against the tight level-1 capacity in [E8] and the weak prefix signal in [E11]. Measured curvature/weight derivations: DEMARGIN c=atanh(0.5)^2=0.3017 (RMS vector to ball norm 0.5), w = measured mean half-margin (distance units) but over all 256 codes with a 3w clamp that can exceed the local bisector margin; pmi c=(0.5/s)^2 (same construction) with w = 0.10 * mean min_k D_k, an explicit 10% cap; GEOMARGIN c=1 default, w = 0.1 * Dbar / rms(z) (10% cap) but z frozen from a pre-pass that never sees the moving encoder; BEABLATE c=0.25 with typical sqrt(c)||u||~0.23 (near-Euclidean) and lambda=1/72000 (one e-fold over the whole 72k-step budget) plus a chosen w=0.25; l1pdo c=1 and w = beta = 0.25 (the commitment weight), i.e. not a distance-scale quantity.
